skill.name: error-recovery

content.value_statement: Subagent workflows can stall when errors, unclear requirements, or contract issues appear. This skill gives retry, context, split, escalation, and abort patterns.
actual_capabilities: Classifies subagent failures as transient, context gap, complexity, boundary, or fatal.
Provides retry, context enhancement, scope reduction, escalation, and abort strategies.
Shows a decision tree for choosing the next recovery action.
Defines retry state tracking examples for failed and running tasks.
Maps blocked reasons to escalation targets such as contract resolver or architect.
limitations: Does not execute recovery automatically; it provides decision patterns.
Assumes workflows use Task subagents and state tracking.
Does not validate produced outputs or contracts by itself.
Does not include scripts, tests, or automation files.

use_cases.title: Recover Multi-Agent Workflows
use_cases.description: Use structured retry and escalation choices when one subagent fails inside a larger workflow.

use_cases.title: Improve Coding Agent Reliability
use_cases.description: Give Claude, Codex, or Claude Code a clear response plan for timeout, confusion, and partial work.

use_cases.title: Standardize Failure Reports
use_cases.description: Create consistent recovery notes when repeated attempts fail and a task needs redesign.

prompt_templates.title: Retry a Transient Failure
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner recovery after timeout or empty output.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the error-recovery skill. A subagent timed out and returned no useful output. Classify the failure and recommend the next retry step.

prompt_templates.title: Add Missing Context
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the error-recovery skill. The previous subagent said the task was unclear. Recommend what context to add before the next attempt.

prompt_templates.title: Split a Large Task
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the error-recovery skill. A broad task produced partial work and then failed. Break the remaining work into smaller subagent tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Escalate a Blocked Task
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced recovery for boundary or contract issues.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the error-recovery skill. A task is blocked by a boundary or contract issue. Choose the escalation path and define the resolution request.

output_examples.input: A subagent timed out and returned no output.
output_examples.output: Classifies the issue as transient. Recommends a simple retry, tracks the attempt count, and stops after three failed attempts.

output_examples.input: An implementer says the requirements are unclear and asks questions in its output.
output_examples.output: Classifies the issue as a context gap. Recommends adding related files, examples, and clarification before retrying.

output_examples.input: A task reports a boundary violation and cannot continue.
output_examples.output: Classifies the issue as boundary or contract related. Recommends escalation to a contract resolver with the blocked reason and affected contract paths.

best_practices: Classify the failure before choosing a recovery action.
Preserve partial work and add exact context for the next attempt.
Stop after repeated failed recovery and produce a clear report.
anti_patterns: Retrying the same broad task without using the failure category.
Escalating every failure before trying an appropriate recovery step.
Discarding partial work when scope reduction can reuse it.

faq.question: Does this skill run commands?
faq.answer: No. It is a Markdown workflow guide and only declares Read and Task tools.

faq.question: Which failures does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers transient errors, context gaps, complexity, boundary issues, and fatal repeated failures.

faq.question: Can it work with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows that use subagents.

faq.question: Does it decide when to stop retrying?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends stopping after repeated failed strategies and creating a failure report.

faq.question: Does it replace a verifier?
faq.answer: No. It helps recover failed tasks, but separate verification should review completed work.

faq.question: Is it only for coding tasks?
faq.answer: No. It can guide any subagent workflow, but its examples focus on software delivery.
